newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan president inspects troops in turbulent south.
newsitem.headline: Sudan president inspects troops in turbulent south.

text.p: Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir has toured towns and inspected forward army positions in southern Sudan, a region where the government has been fighting rebels since 1983.

State television reported on Sunday that Bashir, dressed in military fatigues, inspected troops and attended prayers in the main southern town of Juba to mark the end of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan.
It showed him greeting civilians in Torit, southeast of Juba. It was Bashir's first visit to Torit in years and comes during an apparent lull in fighting in the Blue Nile state in Sudan's southeast.

Sudan has accused Ethiopia, Eritrea and Uganda of military involvement in a rebel offensive launched a month ago from the south and east by the Sudan People's Liberation Army and allied opposition forces. The three countries deny participating.
The Sudan government-owned Al-Sudan Al-Hadith daily said last week that invading Ethiopian troops have started withdrawing heavy weapons from the key border town of Kurmuk.
The Islamist government admits to the fall of the southeast town which recently witnessed sporadic fighting between government forces and the Sudanese opposition forces.
